scenarios.draft: Test the retrieval of a paginated and filtered list of notification settings as an administrator. Verify the endpoint returns correct pagination metadata, supports filters (by key, value, creation or update date), and that only users with admin privileges can access all records, including sensitive settings. Provide both a successful case (with valid pagination and various filter parameters) and failures: unauthorized request, invalid filter format, and attempt to access sensitive entries as a non-admin. Validate edge cases such as empty result set and out-of-range page number.

dependencies.purpose: Creates test notification setting entries for search and filter scenarios. Requires admin privileges.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching details of a notification setting by ID as an admin. Confirm that for an existing setting, all fields are returned accurately and access is authorized. Include negative cases: requesting a non-existent ID (expect not found error), and access denied for non-admin roles or if attempting to access a sensitive/hidden setting without privileges.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure there are notification settings in the system to retrieve for detail view and error path setup.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of a new notification setting by an admin. Cover the standard workflow: set a unique key, value, and description; confirm that the record is created and all metadata fields are correctly returned. Then, attempt to create another notification setting with the same key and confirm the system rejects it with a duplicate key error. Verify proper field validation for required and optional fields; include a case where required data is missing (expect validation error).

Test updating an existing notification setting by ID as an admin. Start by creating a notification setting, then update its value and description, and confirm changes are reflected in the response. Attempt to change the key to another key that already exists and ensure the system rejects it with a duplicate key error. Test validation failures for missing or malformed attributes. Include forbidden error if a non-admin attempts to update.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure at least two notification settings exist—one as the update target and one as a duplicate key source for constraint error testing.

scenarios.draft: Test the soft delete of a notification setting by its ID as an admin and ensure the record is marked as deleted but not physically removed. Attempt to fetch the deleted record after deletion: verify it's hidden from normal listing unless admin queries with special filters. Validate forbidden error for deletes by non-admin users, and error for deleting a non-existent or already-deleted ID.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification setting to test the normal and error deletion cases.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve a paginated and filtered list of discussion board members. Begin by creating multiple member accounts to ensure list population. As an authenticated admin, send a request with pagination preferences and search/filter options (such as username or email search). Confirm that results are paginated correctly, search filters are respected, and all returned members match the query criteria. Also verify that pagination metadata (e.g., total count, current page) is accurate. Edge cases: handle empty result sets, and invalid pagination parameters (such as negative page numbers) to ensure proper error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Create several discussion board member accounts to populate the dataset for realistic search and pagination testing.
Assign admin privileges to a test account so it can access the member listing endpoint.

scenarios.draft: Verify admin or moderator can retrieve a specific member's full details by their unique ID. Scenario: Register a member, promote a user to admin or moderator, then retrieve the created member's details by ID. Confirm all member attributes are returned as expected. Validate error responses when the member ID does not exist or the requesting user lacks authorization. Edge: attempt fetching a deleted or inactive member to confirm access is denied and appropriate error/status is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new discussion board member to serve as the target for retrieval.
Assign admin privileges so the requesting user has authorization to access member details.

scenarios.draft: Test account creation with valid, complete input (unique username, email, display name, secure password), verifying the member is created with an active status and all required fields are stored. Then attempt creation with duplicate username, duplicate email, and missing required fields to check that validation errors are properly enforced and appropriate error codes/messages are returned.

Ensure that an admin can update another member's profile details (display name, email, password), with all constraints enforced. Prepare: create a member, promote requester to admin. Perform: update the member's display name and email to new valid values and expect the changes to persist. Try updating with an existing email (should trigger uniqueness error). Attempt a forbidden update (e.g., change username, or by non-admin): should fail with an error. Test updating a non-existent member and expect a not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member whose profile will be updated in this scenario.
Promote the requester to admin to provide the required permissions for profile update.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can delete a member account (soft- or hard-delete per business rules), causing their membership to become inactive or removed, and that appropriate audit actions occur. Prepare: register a target member, promote the requester to admin. Action: delete the member and attempt to fetch the member again (should yield not found or inactive response). Attempt to delete a non-existent member and expect a not found error. Try deletion by a user without admin permissions; should result in a forbidden/unauthorized error.

dependencies.purpose: Register the member to be deleted in this scenario.
Grant admin privileges to perform the member deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of post edits with pagination, filter, and search parameters. A member creates a post, performs several edits, and then uses this endpoint to fetch post edits filtered by post ID and editor, with pagination. The response should include only the appropriate edits, respect page size, and provide correct pagination metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new discussion board member to act as the post author and editor.
Create a new board to enable post creation in a specific discussion area.
Create an initial post that will be edited to generate post edit history.
Perform one or more edits on the created post so the edit history exists for testing list and search functionality.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching a specific post edit by its ID. First, create a member and a post, perform an edit, and fetch the edit using its ID. Validate that all details are correct. Test failure modes by querying with a random non-existent ID and with an ID that was deleted, expecting appropriate 404 or error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member who will create and edit the post.
Create a discussion board for the post.
Create a post to be edited.
Edit the post in order to generate a post edit record for this test.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of new post edit records. Scenario covers: (1) Normal creation where a member edits an existing post, (2) Attempting to create an edit for a non-existent post, (3) Attempting an edit by a member not authorized to edit this post. Expect validation errors for invalid cases and success otherwise. Check audit fields like timestamps and editor linkage.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least two members to represent the original author and a separate user for authorization testing.
Provision a board to enable post creation.
Create a post that will serve as the base for edit attempts.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing post edit record. Covers: (1) Editor successfully updating their own edit summary, (2) Unauthorized user attempting an update, (3) Invalid update requests such as editing summary to empty or exceeding max length. Check that only allowed fields change and audit trails update accordingly.

dependencies.purpose: Register at least two members: one as the original post edit creator and one as an unauthorized actor.
Create a discussion board to hold posts and edits.
Create a post for edit history.
Create a post edit record to be updated in these scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting a post edit record by its ID. (1) Editor can delete their own edit, (2) Admin/moderator can delete any edit, (3) Unauthorized user cannot delete, (4) Attempt to delete a non-existent or already-deleted edit. Validate audit behavior and response codes for each case.

dependencies.purpose: Register at least three members: one as the edit creator, one as an admin/mod, and one as an unauthorized user.
Create a board to allow post and edit testing.
Create a post to be edited.
Create at least one post edit record to test deletion scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve a paginated and filtered list of admin assignments. Ensure that queries with multiple filter combinations (such as appointment status, date range, appointing admin ID, or assigned member ID) return valid results matching filter criteria. Also test that pagination metadata is correct and edge cases such as empty result sets, page bounds, or invalid filter syntax are properly handled. This scenario requires at least one admin and several admin assignments; setup members and create admin assignments as dependencies.

dependencies.purpose: Create member accounts eligible for admin role assignments in order to produce a dataset that can be queried.
Create admin assignments for members to support verification of listing, search, and pagination filters.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving an admin assignment record by a valid ID as an admin user, confirming that the result contains all fields and correct metadata. Test failure cases: (a) using an invalid or non-existent ID should return a 404, and (b) attempting to access a restricted record as a non-admin should return permission denial. Also confirm that retrieving a revoked or deleted assignment behaves correctly according to business rules (e.g., hidden for non-admins).

dependencies.purpose: Set up one or more member records to receive admin assignments.
Assign the admin role to members so that their admin assignment record can be retrieved by ID.

scenarios.draft: Test admin creation of a new admin assignment for a member. Success scenario: assign admin to an eligible member, verify assignment details (timestamps, references). Failure scenarios: (a) attempt assignment to a non-existent member, (b) assign admin role to an already assigned admin (duplicate admin record), and (c) unauthorized creation by a non-admin user. Also cover unique constraints and audit log creation. Verify appropriate error codes and messages for all business rule or validation violations.

dependencies.purpose: Create member records which will be candidates for admin role assignment.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing admin assignment by ID as an authorized admin: modify fields such as appointing admin, revocation timestamp, or audit notes. Confirm that changes are reflected in the updated record and all audit logs. Test failure scenarios: (a) attempt update with a non-existent or soft-deleted ID, (b) try to set a duplicate unique field, (c) perform update as a non-admin (permission denied). Validate error handling and business constraints are enforced strictly.

dependencies.purpose: Set up the member which will receive the admin role.
Create an admin assignment record that can be updated in this scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test that an authorized admin can successfully delete (revoke) an admin assignment using its ID, and that the action is logged per audit requirements. Confirm that after deletion, the assignment is marked as revoked/soft-deleted and no longer appears in the active list. Also verify (a) deleting with an invalid or already deleted ID returns proper error, and (b) non-admin users receive permission denied errors. Ensure all business logic for referential cleanup or related log updates are satisfied.

dependencies.purpose: Create member records for admin role assignment.
Assign admin role to a member so its assignment can be deleted for the test.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a paginated and filtered list of report categories for moderation workflows. Steps: As an authenticated moderator or admin, request a list of report categories with specific pagination and search criteria (e.g., search for 'spam' or 'abuse'), and verify the expected categories and total count are correct. Include validation for the proper handling of pagination boundaries and empty search results. Confirm that unauthorized roles cannot retrieve the category list.

Test fetching a single report category by its unique ID. Scenario: As an admin, retrieve an existing report category and verify all expected metadata is correctly returned. Negative case: Attempt to fetch with a non-existent UUID and confirm that a proper 'not found' error is returned. Validate access permissions for non-admin users are enforced if necessary.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test report category to obtain a valid ID for fetching.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of a new report category, ensuring all business validations are enforced. Steps: As an admin, create a category with a unique name and a descriptive value, verify details in the response. Then, attempt to create another report category with the same name and confirm that a duplicate name error is returned. Also validate permission restrictions by attempting creation as a non-admin user.

Test updating a report category's name and description. Scenario: As an admin, update the category's name and description and confirm changes reflect in the response. Validate business rules by attempting to update the name to one that already exists and check for error. Also, attempt to update as a non-admin and ensure a permission denied error occurs. Ensure non-existent IDs return a not found error as well.

dependencies.purpose: Create two report categories to test name uniqueness during update operations.

scenarios.draft: Test deletion of report categories according to business rules. Scenario: As an admin, attempt to delete a category that is not referenced by any unresolved reports and verify the category is deleted (or soft-deleted per policy). Negative case: Attempt to delete a category that is currently referenced by unresolved reports and confirm deletion is blocked by a business rule error. Also, check deletion with non-existent ID and confirm not found error is returned. Attempt deletion with insufficient privileges and assert permission is denied.

dependencies.purpose: Create a report category to test deletion and check behavior when referenced in reports.
Create an unresolved report using the test category to simulate in-use category scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filterable list of moderation appeal decisions as an admin or moderator. The test should set up multiple appeal decisions across different outcomes, actors, and appeals by first creating appeals, actions, and users using the necessary endpoints. Verify that filters (by decision outcome, actor, appeal ID, creation date, etc.) work as expected, that only authorized roles (moderator/admin) can access this endpoint, and that unauthorized access is properly denied. Edge cases to test: empty results when filters match nothing, out-of-bounds pagination, and handling of malformed filter parameters (should return appropriate errors).

dependencies.purpose: Create several moderation appeals for test filtering and data setup.
Create appeal decisions with varying outcomes, actors, and related appeals to ensure realistic filter scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching a single moderation appeal decision by its unique ID as the appealing member, assigned moderator, admin, and as an unrelated user. Verify that the appealing member can see their own appeal decision, while access by moderator/admin follows permissions. Confirm that unauthorized users are denied access. Also, verify error responses for non-existent IDs and forbidden attempts. Use appeal and appeal decision creation endpoints to set up data for each access pattern.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation appeal by a member for assignment to a decision.
Create an appeal decision for the specific appeal to test retrieval by ID.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new moderation appeal decision as an authorized moderator or admin. Use a valid appeal ID that is currently undecided. Attempt to create a decision for an already decided appeal and verify that the system rejects duplicate decisions with an appropriate error. Also verify input validation by omitting required fields or submitting invalid enum values for decision outcome. On success, confirm the decision is recorded, the appeal status is updated, and a notification is triggered to the appealant (if system supports notification). Dependency on existing appeal and moderator/admin actor setup.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new moderation appeal in an undecided state for assigning a decision to test valid creation.

scenarios.draft: Test updating the rationale or outcome of a moderation appeal decision as the original deciding moderator or admin before finalization (e.g., before status is locked as finalized). Attempt update by non-deciding actors and after finalization/lock, and verify that only authorized and valid cases are allowed. Check input validation on the update body. Error conditions should include not-found IDs, unauthorized actors, attempts after finalization, or invalid enum values.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation appeal to serve as a basis for a new appeal decision.
Create a new appeal decision that can then be updated during the test.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting (withdrawing) a moderation appeal decision as the original actor (moderator/admin) before finalization/lock, and verify that deletion is forbidden for non-owners, after finalization, and for non-existent appeal decisions. Ensure that deleted entries are soft-deleted and preserved for audit. Confirm proper error responses for invalid or forbidden requests, and test that related status transitions are handled correctly.

dependencies.purpose: Create an appeal and corresponding appeal decision for deletion test.
Create an appeal decision to then attempt deletion by different actors and states.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of discussion board comments as an authenticated member. First, create a user and authenticate. Then, create a board, a post, and several comments (including different nesting depths, authors, and edit flags). Perform search queries with various filters such as specific post ID, thread ID, author ID, comment depth, and date ranges, ensuring that only non-deleted comments are returned by default. Confirm pagination works as intended and that invalid filters (e.g., non-existent post ID, malformed UUIDs) result in appropriate error responses. Also, verify that admin filter options can expose soft-deleted comments if applied by an admin user.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member (user) for authentication and authoring comments.
Create a board to support post and comment creation.
Create a post to which comments will be attached.
Create comments for search and filter testing, representing various depths and authors.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching the full detail of a single comment as an authenticated user. Create a member, a board, a post, and a comment. Retrieve the comment by its ID and verify all expected fields (author, body, post/thread association, timestamps, depth, etc.) are correct. Confirm access is allowed only for authenticated users and that a 404 (not found) is returned for invalid, deleted, or non-existent comment IDs. Additionally, verify that soft-deleted comments are inaccessible to regular users but, if tested as an admin, are accessible for audit purposes.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to own the comment.
Create a board to host the post.
Create a post for the comment.
Create a new comment to be retrieved in the detail scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new comment on a post as an authenticated user. Register a user, create a board, post, and, optionally, a thread. Attempt to create a root-level and a reply comment (with various valid nesting/depth, post/thread linkage). Validate successful creation (response includes fully populated comment entity), required field enforcement, and that default flags (edit/soft delete) are correctly set. Confirm that comments cannot be created if the post is locked or the referenced post/thread/author doesn't exist, and that business rules such as content guidelines are enforced, returning errors for violations.

dependencies.purpose: Register a user to serve as the comment author.
Create a board to support the post.
Create a post to attach comments to.

scenarios.draft: Test editing an existing comment as the author. Register a user and create a board, post, and comment. Attempt to edit the comment, changing its body and possibly thread/depth, and check that the update succeeds. Ensure the edit flag is set and that changes are logged for audit. Try editing a comment as a different (non-author) user and confirm permission is denied. Ensure edits fail for locked, already deleted, or non-existent comments, and for content rule violations (e.g., banned words), returning correct errors. Also, test moderation/admin override for editing others' comments.

dependencies.purpose: Register original comment author and a possible second member for unauthorized-edit tests.
Create a board.
Create the parent post.
Create the comment to be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test soft-deleting a comment as its owner and as an admin (if business rules permit). Register a user, create a board, post, and comment. Delete the comment and confirm it is no longer returned in standard comment listings and its deleted_at is set. Try to delete as a different member and confirm a permission denied error. Attempt to delete an already deleted or non-existent comment and verify correct error handling. Check whether admins or moderators can delete others' comments (when permitted). Verify audit logs and that deletion triggers proper system events (e.g., comment disappears from UI).

dependencies.purpose: Register both the original comment author and, if permitted, an admin user for role-based tests.
Create a board.
Create a post.
Create the comment to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated list of discussion posts with default or minimal filtering. Ensure the response contains post summaries, pagination metadata, and that valid, non-empty result sets are returned for boards with existing posts. Verify edge case with empty board returns an empty result and correct pagination metadata. Member authentication (at minimum) is required to access this endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Create a discussion board to which posts can be attached.
Register a member who can create posts and list them.
Create posts associated to the board and member for listing tests.

scenarios.draft: Test listing posts with advanced filters (e.g., filtering by board, author, date range) and sorting (e.g., by creation date desc). Verify that only matching posts are returned and sorting follows the query parameter. Test invalid filter parameters result in error responses. Authenticated member context is required for post access; must ensure setup of several posts with diverse attributes.

dependencies.purpose: Create different boards for post association.
Register several members to author various posts.
Create multiple posts with varied attributes (board, author, time) for filter coverage.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching detailed information of a discussion post by valid post ID. The requester should be authenticated with at least member role. Ensure all expected fields (title, author, board, timestamps, etc.) are populated and correct. Must verify that the returned data matches the record created earlier.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to author a post and make the API call as authenticated context.
Create a discussion board for post association.
Create the post and fetch its ID for the GET test.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a post with a nonexistent or random UUID. Confirm the response returns a not found error (404) and no sensitive information is leaked. Authenticated as regular member is sufficient.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to act as API caller for context.

scenarios.draft: Test successfully creating a new discussion post with all required fields (title, body, author, valid board). Authenticated as member, the resulting post should be returned with all standard fields filled, and be visible in board listing/endpoints. Also verify timestamps and references are correct.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to be the post's author and perform authenticated calls.
Create a board to which the post will be attached.

scenarios.draft: Test post creation failure when provided board ID does not exist or is deleted. Expect error response indicating invalid board. This validates referential integrity enforcement. Member authentication required.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for authoring the post and request context.

scenarios.draft: Test a member updating their own post—modifying title and body with valid inputs. Expect post properties to update, 'updated_at' timestamp to change, and edit to be reflected in subsequent get requests. Must ensure thread is not locked.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate the member who will author and later edit the post.
Create a discussion board for post association.
Create a post as this member to later update.

scenarios.draft: Test update attempt by a member who is not the original post author. Expect error response for lack of permission (403). Moderator or admin not involved. Must set up two different members and authenticate the non-author for this test.

dependencies.purpose: Register two members, one for authoring the post and another for unauthorized update attempt.
Create a discussion board for post association.
Create a post as the first member for update attempt by the second.

scenarios.draft: Test successful soft deletion of a post by its original author. The deleted post should be inaccessible to further get/list calls, except to admins/moderators if business rules specify. Verify that 'deleted_at' or similar attributes are set and deletion is logged. Requires authentication as post author.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to create and delete their own post.
Create a board for the post.
Create a post as the member for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test soft-delete attempt by a member who is not the post's author. Expect error for insufficient permissions, and that the post remains accessible. Requires two members and authentication as the non-author.

dependencies.purpose: Register two members, one to author a post, another to attempt unauthorized deletion.
Create a board for post association.
Create the post with the first member for deletion attempt by the second.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of moderator assignments using different filters such as active/revoked status, assigned date ranges, promoted_by_admin_id, and member_id. Begin with a system where several moderator assignments exist with different attributes (e.g., some active, some revoked, some assigned by different admins). Verify that the correct assignments are returned for each filter combination and pagination scenario. Confirm that proper permissions are enforced: only admins and moderators can access the full list. Attempt to retrieve using invalid filters or insufficient permissions and confirm appropriate error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Create several member accounts that can be assigned as moderators or used as filter candidates.
Assign various moderator roles to the created members using different assigner admins and different assignment periods, setting up data for varied search cases.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving detailed information for a single moderator assignment by valid and invalid ID. Start by creating a member and assigning them as a moderator. With valid admin or moderator credentials, retrieve the moderator assignment details using its ID and verify all expected audit and relational fields are present. Also, attempt to retrieve a non-existent moderator ID or one the user does not have access to, and confirm correct error handling for not found or unauthorized access.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member whose ID will be assigned as a moderator.
Assign the registered member as a moderator and extract the assignment ID for retrieval testing.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a new moderator assignment and handling of assignment conflicts or constraint violations. First, create at least one normal member and one admin. As the admin, assign the member as a moderator and verify that the new assignment is returned with correct links to member/admin IDs and timestamps. Attempt to assign the same member as a moderator again (without revoking previous assignment) to verify the unique single-assignment constraint triggers an error. Also test creation with a non-existent member or with insufficient privilege (e.g., by a non-admin) and check for appropriate validation or permission errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create member accounts to participate in moderator assignment scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing moderator assignment's properties, such as changing the assigner admin or revocation timestamp. Workflow: create an admin, a member, and assign the member as a moderator. Then, as a different admin, update the assignment to set a revocation time or adjust assigner. Confirm that audit trails are correctly updated. Attempt to update using duplicate assignment info or invalid state changes to trigger business rule errors. Also, test updating as a non-admin to ensure permission is denied.

dependencies.purpose: Register multiple members and an admin, to set up both moderator and assigner candidates.
Assign a moderator role to one member for update testing.

scenarios.draft: Test revoking (soft-deleting) a moderator assignment for different business scenarios. Begin by assigning a member as moderator through an admin. As the admin, revoke the assignment and ensure the record is marked accordingly and all privilege-removal audit trails are triggered. Attempt to delete an assignment that has already been revoked to confirm correct error behavior. Try deleting as an unauthorized user or with an invalid ID and verify permission/validation errors. Check that post-revocation, the member no longer has moderator access in downstream API operations.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to be assigned as a moderator.
Assign moderator role to the member, retrieving the assignment ID for downstream revoke/delete operations.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated list of discussion board channels with optional search and filter criteria (such as by name or description). Validate that only non-deleted and active channels are returned in a standard user query, and verify pagination, sorting (by creation date), and handling of malformed filter parameters. Attempt both successful queries and queries with intentionally malformed filters to check error responses. Consider access as a regular authenticated member and as an admin requesting soft-deleted channels.

dependencies.purpose: Create several channels to ensure the list endpoint returns meaningful pagination and filtering results during testing.

scenarios.draft: Test that regular authenticated users do NOT see soft-deleted channels in the channel list, but admins with sufficient rights (using appropriate filters) can view including soft-deleted channels. Verify that attempts to use admin-only filters as a non-admin are rejected with the appropriate error message.

dependencies.purpose: Create both active and then delete some channels to create soft-deleted records for permission testing purposes.
Soft-delete selected channels as admin for restricted retrieval, ensuring that deleted channels are present for downstream list testing.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching channel details for an existing channel as a regular member, as a moderator, and as an admin. Verify normal (non-deleted, active) channel details are accessible for all, but that non-active, soft-deleted, or hidden channels are only visible to admins or moderators. Ensure attempts to access restricted channels by normal users result in access denied errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create channels with both normal (active) and soft-deleted (admin) states for completeness of permission testing.
Soft-delete channel(s) for permission testing regarding restricted view.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to fetch channel details using a randomly generated or non-existent UUID. Verify the system correctly returns a not found error in compliance with error handling policies.

Test successful channel creation by an administrative user with a unique name and valid data. Validate all required fields, and confirm that the new channel is initialized as non-deleted and active with correct metadata populated.

Test failure scenario when an admin attempts to create a channel with a name that already exists (violating database uniqueness constraint). Validate that the correct error code and message are returned.

dependencies.purpose: First, create a channel with a unique name to set up the duplicate scenario. Then, attempt to create another channel using the same name to test for conflict handling.

scenarios.draft: Test that non-admin users (members, moderators) attempting to create a channel are denied with a permission error. Attempt channel creation as a regular user and as a moderator, and confirm that only admins can create new channels.

Test updating selected attributes (such as name and description) of an existing channel as an admin, confirming that all updates are logged for audit, constraints are maintained (e.g., name uniqueness), and normalized values are accepted. Confirm the response contains the updated entity.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial channel for update testing.

scenarios.draft: Test that updating a channel's name to a value already in use by another existing channel fails with a duplicate name error. Admins should receive a clear error message and no data corruption should occur.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least two channels: one for attempted update and another to create the name conflict scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test that non-admin users (members or moderators) attempting to update a channel are denied with an appropriate permission error. Validate that only admins are allowed to perform update operations.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel to serve as the update target.

scenarios.draft: Test successful soft-deletion of a channel by an admin. Confirm that the response returns the pre-deletion entity data and that the 'deleted_at' timestamp is populated. Ensure that deleted channels are hidden from standard user queries but visible to admins via specific filters.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel to serve as the target for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test that a non-admin user (member or moderator) attempting to soft-delete a channel is denied with the appropriate error message. Validate that only admins are authorized to perform channel deletions.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel as the deletion target.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to delete a channel that was already soft-deleted. Confirm that the system correctly returns an error, preventing double-deletion or inconsistent state.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel, then soft-delete it to set up the test condition.
Soft-delete the channel before attempting a second deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of post snapshots using various filters and pagination options. First, create a member, a board, a post, and a snapshot. Then, attempt to fetch a paginated list of snapshots filtered by post ID, creator ID, or date range, ensuring only the appropriate snapshots are included and pagination metadata is correct. Expect filtered results, valid pagination, and appropriate response structure.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to act as the post author and snapshot creator.
Set up a board for the post to belong to.
Create a post to which snapshots will refer. Requires an existing member and board.
Create at least one snapshot to ensure there is snapshot data to retrieve in list.

scenarios.draft: Test listing post snapshots using an invalid filter (e.g., malformed post ID or unsupported filter value). Verify that the system returns an error or empty result, and the error message or response format is clear and informative.

Ensure that the list endpoint does not return soft-deleted (archived) snapshots to regular non-admin searches. First, create and then delete a post snapshot. Then, list snapshots and confirm the deleted snapshot does not appear in the result set.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member for snapshot creation.
Set up a discussion board.
Create a post for snapshots.
Create a post snapshot.
Soft-delete the created post snapshot prior to searching for it.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a post snapshot by valid ID. Prepare by creating member, board, post, and post snapshot. Fetch the snapshot by its returned ID and confirm all fields reflect the snapshot's attributes accurately.

event.review:
The test plan attempts to simulate a uniqueness conflict by updating confB's key to match confA's key, but according to the DTOs and the API, configurations can only have their value and (optionally) description updated—they cannot update the configuration key.

Thus, per the current endpoint specs and DTOs provided:
- The POST /discussionBoard/configurations endpoint requires a unique 'key' when creating a configuration.
- The PUT /discussionBoard/configurations/{id} endpoint only allows updating the 'value' and 'description', not the 'key'.

Therefore, the uniqueness constraint on 'key' can only be tested on create, not on update. The scenario is not implementable as described, given the API function and DTO definitions; the update endpoint will never allow changing a configuration's key, so there is no way to trigger a uniqueness conflict on 'key' by updating an existing configuration.

However, for the sake of completeness, I implemented the function with an explanatory note highlighting that the test may not be executable if the backend matches the DTO and endpoint spec. The test will attempt to update value/description, but this will never involve a unique key check, so no conflict will occur. Thus, the only truly testable scenario here is to try to update a configuration that does not exist or with non-updatability edge cases—not unique key update conflict.

If API supports key update in reality (not reflected in the DTOs), then the test would require changing the body schema accordingly. Otherwise, the uniqueness constraint on key is only relevant for POST, not PUT.
